reference: The runnable contract expectations use Bash's documented type/help builtins and the loadable's documented short synopsis (curl_struct.short_doc), independent of any curl transfer output. Transfer parity is claimed only for the loopback redirect case. Deferred operation comparisons require curl plus a separately authored deterministic HTTP/TLS fixture in a future disposable VM with private networking; the fixture should capture request bytes and derive responses independently. The redirect-location-control-bytes case runs Debian curl and the builtin against the same private loopback peer inside the fixture's network namespace; the peer logs each request line it receives.
coverage: Bash classifies curl as a shell builtin when PATH is empty.
Bash type output identifies the command as a shell builtin.
Bash short help exposes the documented curl synopsis.
Deferred: HTTP body framing, request construction, file output, HTTP errors, redirects, and HTTPS certificate behavior.
Parser-only missing option arguments and unknown option status/diagnostics against external curl.
Redirect Location hygiene against a private loopback peer: bare CR/LF, control bytes, spaces, high bytes, trailing blanks and NUL.
exclusions: Apart from the loopback redirect cases, no transfer command is executed; parser-only errors return before URL or network handling.
The HTTP and HTTPS operation cases are DEFERRED and have not passed; each requires a disposable VM or isolated mock service and a GNU curl reference.

cases.purpose: Bash's type -t contract reports the compiled-in curl command as a builtin even with an empty executable search path.
Bash's type contract describes curl as a shell builtin rather than resolving an external executable.
Bash short help publishes the documented synopsis registered by the curl loadable.
Compare response body bytes and status for Content-Length and chunked HTTP responses, including a small binary body with NUL and high-bit bytes.
Check request method, path, headers, POST body, Basic authorization, and cookie handling against a captured request from a deterministic server.
Compare -o output bytes, -O URL basename handling, -D dumped headers, and -w %{http_code} output including resulting fixture files.
Check ordinary HTTP error responses with and without -f, including curl's status 22 behavior and -sS diagnostic policy.
Check -L handling of absolute and relative Location values, redirect limits, and a bounded long redirect target.

A private loopback peer sends Location values holding a bare LF or CR (ends the header line), a control byte in an absolute target (exit 3, nothing requested), a control byte, space or high byte in a relative target (percent-encoded), trailing blanks (dropped) and a NUL (exit 8). No raw control byte reaches the next request line, which the peer logs.
cases.script:
cat > srv.py <<'PY'
import select, socket, sys
# Loopback HTTP peer: A is 127.0.0.1:18080, A2 is 127.0.0.1:18082 (same host,
# other port), B is 127.0.0.2:18081 (other host). ROUTE=LOCATION arguments
# make PORT/PATH answer 302 with that Location (Python escapes allowed); every
# other path answers 200 "ok". Logs each request line and which credential
# headers it carried, and exits after a path starting /end or 1.5 idle seconds.
routes = {}
for a in sys.argv[1:]:
    k, v = a.split('=', 1)
    routes[k] = v.encode('latin-1').decode('unicode_escape').encode('latin-1')
socks = []
for host, port in (('127.0.0.1', 18080), ('127.0.0.2', 18081), ('127.0.0.1', 18082)):
    s = socket.socket()
    s.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
    s.bind((host, port))
    s.listen(4)
    socks.append(s)
print('ready', flush=True)
log = open('log', 'w')
while True:
    r, _, _ = select.select(socks, [], [], 1.5)
    if not r:
        break
    c, _ = r[0].accept()
    with c:
        c.settimeout(5)
        d = b''
        while b'\r\n\r\n' not in d:
            x = c.recv(4096)
            if not x:
                break
            d += x
        line = d.split(b'\r\n')[0]
        parts = line.split(b' ')
        path = parts[1].decode('latin-1') if len(parts) > 1 else ''
        names = sorted({l.split(b':')[0].decode('latin-1').lower() for l in d.split(b'\r\n')[1:] if b':' in l}
                       & {'authorization', 'cookie'})
        port = r[0].getsockname()[1]
        log.write('%d %r %s\n' % (port, line, ' '.join(names) or '-'))
        log.flush()
        loc = routes.get('%d%s' % (port, path))
        if loc is not None:
            c.sendall(b'HTTP/1.1 302 Found\r\nLocation: ' + loc + b'\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n')
        else:
            c.sendall(b'HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 3\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\nok\n')
            if path.startswith('/end'):
                break
PY
coproc SRV { /usr/bin/python3 srv.py '18080/s=http://127.0.0.2:18081/end\nX-Injected: 1'; }
read -r -t 5 ready <&"${SRV[0]}"
rc=0; curl -s -S --max-time 5 -L http://127.0.0.1:18080/s || rc=$?
wait "$SRV_PID" || true
printf 'run %d: rc=%s\n' 1 "$rc"
cat log
coproc SRV { /usr/bin/python3 srv.py '18080/s=/end\rX-Injected: 1'; }
read -r -t 5 ready <&"${SRV[0]}"
rc=0; curl -s -S --max-time 5 -L http://127.0.0.1:18080/s || rc=$?
wait "$SRV_PID" || true
printf 'run %d: rc=%s\n' 2 "$rc"
cat log

read -r -t 5 ready <&"${SRV[0]}"
rc=0; curl -s -S --max-time 5 -L http://127.0.0.1:18080/s || rc=$?
wait "$SRV_PID" || true
printf 'run %d: rc=%s\n' 3 "$rc"
cat log

read -r -t 5 ready <&"${SRV[0]}"
rc=0; curl -s -S --max-time 5 -L http://127.0.0.1:18080/s || rc=$?
wait "$SRV_PID" || true
printf 'run %d: rc=%s\n' 4 "$rc"
cat log
coproc SRV { /usr/bin/python3 srv.py '18080/s=/end\x01x' ; }
read -r -t 5 ready <&"${SRV[0]}"
rc=0; curl -s -S --max-time 5 -L http://127.0.0.1:18080/s || rc=$?

read -r -t 5 ready <&"${SRV[0]}"
rc=0; curl -s -S --max-time 5 -L http://127.0.0.1:18080/s || rc=$?
